key_insight: Crystal prototype reuse supports materials discovery, but measured family coverage and novelty depend strongly on structural equivalence rules.
engineering_relevance: Prototype libraries can accelerate substitution screening and crystal structure prediction, provided family definitions and training coverage are validated.
method: Compare prototype libraries, construction methods, and structural equivalence rules.
Analyze GraphID family distributions across ICSD, Materials Project, OQMD, and LeMat samples.
Compare 12 generative CSP models and test sensitivity to withheld stoichiometry classes.
evidence_signal: The top 100 families cover 30–67% of sampled structures, 72–82% of observed families are singletons, and template retrieval achieves the highest top-1 success rate in the model comparison.
watch_item: Up to 76% of structures change GraphID with neighbor tolerance; withholding stoichiometry classes does not establish generalization to unseen prototypes.
paper_title: A Comprehensive Survey of Crystal Structural Prototypes: Construction, Classification, and Applications
